subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Continues the school Drive Quran folder progression (TPS Quran Tracker tajweed rules) into Year 9; classical tajweed (Hafs 'an 'Asim) and tadabbur method; Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Madd in recitation and stopping
lessons.title: Year 9 audit: tajweed in Surat Al-Kawthar
objectives: Recall the rules secured in Years 7 and 8
Find rules inside a real surah
Set two tajweed targets for the half term

keywords.def: a check of what you know and where the gaps are
reading a letter heavy, with a full mouth
clear pronunciation of noon sakinah or tanween before a throat letter

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Name the four rules of noon sakinah and tanween.
How many counts does madd lazim take?

teach.heading: Why audit?
bullets: Year 9 builds on every earlier year
Gaps in old rules slow new learning
Honest checking is part of ihsan
teach.note: Welcome pupils warmly. Explain that this half term revises madd and the lam rules, then studies three surahs. Ask: which rule do you feel least secure in? Pupils note it privately. Reassure them that the Prophet's wife A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the one who recites with difficulty has a double reward (Bukhari and Muslim). Effort matters.

teach.heading: Our text: Al-Kawthar
teach.note: Show the three ayat in Arabic: إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ، فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ، إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْأَبْتَرُ. Recite once yourself, then choral. Pupils should already know this surah, so the focus is rules, not memorising.

teach.heading: Rule hunt (1)
bullets: inna: noon with shaddah, so ghunnah
wanhar: noon sakinah before haa, izhar
teach.note: Model the hunt. In وَانْحَرْ the noon is sakinah and the next letter is haa, a throat letter, so izhar halqi. Ask: what would be wrong? Merging the noon into the haa. Common error: pupils nasalise the noon here.

teach.heading: Rule hunt (2)
bullets: al-kawthar: waw sakinah after fatha, no madd
abtar: stopping on raa after fatha-sad, heavy
teach.note: In الْكَوْثَرَ the waw is sakinah after fatha but a voweled thaa follows, so it is simply read, not madd leen. On stopping at أَبْتَرْ, the raa is sakin; the sakin ba before it is passed over and the fatha on the ta decides: heavy. Ask pupils to explain in their own words.

teach.heading: Set targets
teach.note: Pupils write targets in a table: rule, example ayah, how I will practise. Share two aloud. Close with a short dua asking Allah to make the Qur'an the spring of our hearts.

practice: Which rule applies to the noon in وَانْحَرْ, and why?
When you stop on أَبْتَرْ, is the raa heavy or light? Explain.
What does shaddah on noon in إِنَّا require?
independent: Recite Al-Kawthar twice, marking every rule on a printed copy
Complete the audit table: rule, secure/unsure, example
Write two targets with a practice plan
exit: Name one rule you are secure in.
Give one example ayah for a rule you want to improve.
lessons.homework: Practise your two target rules daily with five examples each from surahs you know.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: printed Al-Kawthar with rule key and colour codes. Stretch: write three audit questions for a partner.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Muddaththir and madd in recitation
lessons.title: Madd 'arid lis-sukun and madd leen
lessons.bigQuestion: ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ (74:41): when you continue it is 2 counts; when you stop it can be 6. Why does stopping change it?
objectives: To understand the madd that appear only when stopping ('arid lis-sukun and leen) and choose a consistent length
successCriteria: All: explain why 'arid only happens when stopping
Most: stretch 'arid 2, 4 or 6 and keep it consistent
Some: distinguish madd leen from 'arid at the end of an ayah
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: calm, measured recitation

keywords.def: lengthening a vowel sound, counted in beats (harakat)
a soft و or ي sakinah after fathah

hook.text: ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ (74:41): when you continue it is 2 counts; when you stop it can be 6. Why does stopping change it?
hook.a: Stopping makes the last letter sakin; a madd letter followed by a sukoon can stretch (2, 4 or 6).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4).

starter.q: Recite Al-Muddaththir 74:32 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Stopping changes the word
bullets: At a stop the last letter becomes sakin
A madd letter before it may lengthen
Only when stopping, never when continuing
teach.note: Bismillah. Model 74:41 ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ: continuing (2), stopping (2, 4 or 6).

teach.heading: Madd leen
bullets: و or ي sakinah after fathah
Next letter sakin only because we stop
teach.note: Leen is soft; lips relaxed.

misconception.wrong: Changing the 'arid length at every ayah end
misconception.right: Choose 2, 4 or 6 and keep it for the whole recitation

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: 'Arid only exists when stopping; joined, it is a natural madd of 2.

practice.q: Recite 74:40 to 45 stopping at each ayah end, keeping 4 counts on every 'arid.
practice.a: 'Arid (4 counts) on يَتَسَآءَلُونَ, ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ, ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ, ٱلْمِسْكِينَ, ٱلْخَآئِضِينَ; none on سَقَرَ (no madd letter before the raa).
practice.model: I do: 74:40 يَتَسَآءَلُونَ: stop on noon, و before it: 4. 74:41 ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ: 4. 74:42 سَقَرَ: stop سَقَرْ, no madd letter, so no 'arid.

practice.q: 'Arid lis-sukun can be ...

independent.q: Ending audit (pupil PDF): for 74:38 to 56, mark which ayah endings give 'arid lis-sukun when stopping. Today's rota group recites 74:31 to 37.
independent.a: 'Arid at 74:39, 40, 41, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49. None at 74:38, 42, 50 to 56 (no madd letter before the last letter, or taa marbutah).
independent.model: The teacher marks 74:38 رَهِينَةٌ: stopping gives رَهِينَهْ; the last letter has no madd before it, so no 'arid.

independent.q: Extend: find a madd leen at the end of an ayah in Quraysh.
Stretch: why can 'arid never be less than 2 counts?
independent.a: It is built on a madd letter, which always has its natural 2 counts; stopping can only add to it.

exit.q: Madd leen is a و or ي sakinah after ...
exit.a: fathah

exit.q: Back to our ponder: ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ (74:41): when you continue it is 2 counts; when you stop it can be 6. Why does stopping change it?
exit.a: Stopping makes the last letter sakin; a madd letter followed by a sukoon can stretch (2, 4 or 6).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Muddaththir and madd in recitation
lessons.title: Madd silah and madd 'iwad
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do we read «لَهُۥ» as 'lahoo' but «لَهُ ٱلْ...» as 'lahul'?
objectives: To understand the madd of the pronoun haa (silah) and the madd at a stop on tanween fathah ('iwad), and apply them in Al-Muddaththir
successCriteria: All: read silah sughra as 2 counts
Most: read silah kubra 4 or 5 before hamza
Some: explain when the pronoun haa has no silah
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the fine detail of Arabic grammar preserved in recitation

keywords.def: lengthening a vowel sound, counted in beats (harakat)
the madd on the pronoun haa between two vowels
the alif replacing tanween fathah at a stop
a pronoun, here the haa meaning him or his

hook.text: Why do we read «لَهُۥ» as 'lahoo' but «لَهُ ٱلْ...» as 'lahul'?
hook.a: Silah only happens when the haa is between two vowelled letters; before a sukoon (or hamzat al-wasl) it is short.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recital' (Al-Baqarah 2:121).

starter.q: Recite Al-Muddaththir 74:40 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Madd silah
teach.note: Bismillah. The pronoun haa (him/his) between two vowelled letters gets a small waw or yaa.

teach.heading: No silah
bullets: Letter before the haa is sakin: فِيهِ هُدًى
Next letter is sakin: لَهُ ٱلْمُلْكُ
Stopping on the haa: ذَكَرَهُۥ at a stop (74:55)
teach.note: A few words are special cases in Hafs; the teacher shows them when met.

teach.heading: Madd 'iwad
bullets: The tanween becomes a long aa, 2 counts
Not on taa marbutah (ـةً stops as haa)
teach.note: Al-Muddaththir is full of them: وَحِيدًۭا (74:11) stops as wahidaa; مَّمْدُودًۭا (74:12); شُهُودًۭا (74:13); تَمْهِيدًۭا (74:14); صَعُودًا (74:17).

misconception.right: Stop as 'waheedaa': the tanween becomes a 2-count alif

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Between two vowelled letters, and the next letter is not hamza: sughra, 2 counts.

practice.q: Read 74:11 to 14 stopping at each ayah end; name the silah and 'iwad.
practice.a: Silah sughra: لَهُۥ مَالًۭا (74:12), لَهُۥ تَمْهِيدًۭا (74:14); 'iwad at the stops: وَحِيدَا, مَّمْدُودَا, شُهُودَا, تَمْهِيدَا.
practice.model: I do: 74:11 stop: وَحِيدًا becomes waheedaa ('iwad). 74:12 لَهُۥ مَالًا: silah sughra lahoo, 2; stop مَّمْدُودَا ('iwad).

practice.q: Silah kubra is followed by ...
practice.a: hamza

independent.q: Silah and 'iwad audit (pupil PDF): mark them in 74:11 to 18 and 74:54 to 56. Today's rota group recites 74:38 to 56.
independent.a: Silah sughra: 74:12, 74:14, 74:16 إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ, 74:17 سَأُرْهِقُهُۥ صَعُودًا, 74:18 إِنَّهُۥ فَكَّرَ, 74:54 إِنَّهُۥ تَذْكِرَةٌ; 'iwad at stops: 74:11 to 14, 74:17; 74:55 ذَكَرَهُۥ at a stop: no silah.
independent.model: The teacher marks 74:16: إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ: haa between نَّ (vowel) and ك (vowel): silah sughra, 2.

independent.q: Extend: find a silah kubra in Al-Humazah.
independent.a: مَالَهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَهُۥ (104:3)

independent.q: Stretch: why do we stop on رَهِينَةٌ (74:38) as 'raheenah', not with an alif?
independent.a: It ends in taa marbutah: at a stop it becomes haa sakinah; 'iwad is only for tanween fathah on other letters.

exit.q: Stopping on «صَعُودًا» (74:17) gives ...
exit.a: sa'oodaa ('iwad)

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Why do we read «لَهُۥ» as 'lahoo' but «لَهُ ٱلْ...» as 'lahul'?
exit.a: Silah only happens when the haa is between two vowelled letters; before a sukoon (or hamzat al-wasl) it is short.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Al-Qiyamah, hamzat al-wasl and alif-lam
lessons.title: Alif-lam: shamsiyyah and qamariyyah
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do you think Arabic merges the laam into some letters but not others?
objectives: To understand how the letter after al- decides whether the laam is said or silent
successCriteria: All: sort al- words into sun and moon letters
Most: recite al- words in Al-Qiyamah correctly
Some: explain why the sun-letter laam is merged
lessons.smsc: Intellectual: the logic of Arabic sounds

keywords.def: sun letter: the laam of al- is silent and the next letter doubles
moon letter: the laam of al- is said with a sukoon

hook.text: Why do you think Arabic merges the laam into some letters but not others?
hook.a: The 14 sun letters come from near the laam's place in the mouth, so it merges for ease; the moon letters are far, so the laam stays clear.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4).

starter.q: Recite Al-Qiyamah 75:3 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: The definite article ٱلْ
bullets: Sun: laam silent, shaddah on the next letter
Moon: laam with sukoon, said clearly
teach.note: Bismillah. Model ٱلشَّمْسُ and ٱلْقَمَرُ (75:9).

teach.heading: Sun and moon in Al-Qiyamah
teach.note: Pupils decide first.

teach.heading: Memory phrase
bullets: Moon letters: اِبْغِ حَجَّكَ وَخَفْ عَقِيمَهُ
All the others are sun letters
Check by sight: shaddah after the laam means sun
teach.note: The mushaf shows it: a sukoon on the laam (moon) or a shaddah on the next letter (sun).

teach.heading: The laam in the Name Allah
teach.note: Recap from Year 5: «بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ» (1:1) light after kasrah; «قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ» (112:1) heavy after fathah.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: ن is a sun letter: the laam is silent and the ن doubles.

practice.q: Label al- in «ٱلْمَفَرُّ» (75:10) and «ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ» (75:12).
practice.a: Both moon letters (م): the laam is said: al-mafarr, al-mustaqarr.
practice.model: I do: after the laam is م; the laam has a sukoon in the mushaf: moon letter, so I say al-.

practice.q: Moon letters are in the phrase ...
practice.a: اِبْغِ حَجَّكَ وَخَفْ عَقِيمَهُ

independent.q: Sort (pupil PDF): label every al- in 75:1 to 15 as sun or moon. Today's rota group recites 75:1 to 10.
independent.a: Sun: ٱلنَّفْسِ، ٱللَّوَّامَةِ، ٱلشَّمْسُ; moon: ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ، ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ، ٱلْبَصَرُ، ٱلْقَمَرُ، ٱلْمَفَرُّ، ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ.
independent.model: The teacher labels 75:1: ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ: moon (ق).

independent.q: Extend: how many sun and moon letters are there?
independent.a: Fourteen each.

independent.q: Stretch: why is «ٱللَّوَّامَةِ» a sun letter even though it starts with laam?
independent.a: The laam of al- merges into the laam after it: laam is one of the 14 sun letters.

exit.q: «ٱلشَّمْسُ»: the laam is ...
exit.a: silent

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Why do you think Arabic merges the laam into some letters but not others?
exit.a: The 14 sun letters come from near the laam's place in the mouth, so it merges for ease; the moon letters are far, so the laam stays clear.

lessons.title: Hamzat al-wasl: starting well
lessons.bigQuestion: You stop after 'كَلَّا' in 75:20 and want to restart at 'بَلْ'. Easy. But what if a word starts with ٱ? How do you start?
objectives: To understand how to start on a word that begins with hamzat al-wasl and why it disappears when joined
successCriteria: All: tell hamzat al-wasl (ٱ) from hamzat al-qat' (أ)
Most: choose the right starting vowel for verbs and nouns
Some: start correctly at three places in Al-Qiyamah after a stop
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: starting well, in recitation and in life

keywords.def: a joining hamza: said only when we start with it, dropped when joined

hook.text: You stop after 'كَلَّا' in 75:20 and want to restart at 'بَلْ'. Easy. But what if a word starts with ٱ? How do you start?
hook.a: Hamzat al-wasl is said when starting: with fathah in al-, and with kasrah or dammah in verbs depending on the third letter.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4).

starter.q: Recite Al-Qiyamah 75:21 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

starter.a: a short pause with no breath
options: a short pause with no breath

teach.heading: Two kinds of hamzah
teach.note: Bismillah.

teach.heading: Which vowel to start with
teach.note: Model each.

teach.heading: In Al-Qiyamah
teach.note: Starting points after a stop.

head: If you start at
Say
rows: if started: ittabi' (kasrah: 3rd letter has kasrah)

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Verb; the third letter ه has a fathah, so we start with kasrah: idh-hab.

practice.q: How do you start the word «ٱتَّبِعْ» (as in 75:18) if you begin with it?
practice.a: ittabi': the third letter ب has a kasrah, so start with kasrah.
practice.model: I do: it is a verb. Count letters: ٱ (1), تّ (2), بِ (3): kasrah. So start with kasrah: ittabi'.

practice.q: Al- always starts with ...
practice.a: fathah

independent.q: Starting drill (pupil PDF): write how to start each of eight words with hamzat al-wasl from Al-Qiyamah, Al-Muddaththir and Al-A'la. Today's rota group recites 75:20 to 30.
independent.a: Answers on the teacher sheet (al- words with fathah; verbs by the third letter; ism with kasrah).
independent.model: The teacher does the first: ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ → al-qiyaamah.

independent.q: Extend: why does the alif of «بَلِ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ» disappear in reading?
independent.a: Hamzat al-wasl is dropped when joined; the laam of بَلْ takes a kasrah to join.

independent.q: Stretch: name three special nouns that start with hamzat al-wasl.
independent.a: ٱسْم، ٱبْن، ٱمْرِئ (also ٱبْنَة، ٱمْرَأَة، ٱثْنَان، ٱثْنَتَان).

exit.q: Hamzat al-wasl is said ...
exit.a: only when starting with it

exit.q: Back to our ponder: You stop after 'كَلَّا' in 75:20 and want to restart at 'بَلْ'. Easy. But what if a word starts with ٱ? How do you start?
exit.a: Hamzat al-wasl is said when starting: with fathah in al-, and with kasrah or dammah in verbs depending on the third letter.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Al-'Asr
lessons.title: Surat Al-'Asr: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Surat Al-'Asr accurately
Identify rules in each ayah
Stop and start correctly
starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Kawthar from memory.
Is the lam in الْعَصْرِ shamsiyyah or qamariyyah?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
teach.note: Recite: وَالْعَصْرِ، إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ، إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ. Surah 103. Pupils repeat after you in short chunks. This surah is short but dense with meaning.

teach.heading: Ayah 1 and 2 rules
bullets: khusr: stop on sakin raa, heavy
teach.note: Ayah 2: إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ. The alif of al- is hamzat al-wasl and drops when joined, so we say innal-insana, with ghunnah on inna. The hamzah of insan is a moon letter, so the lam is clear. At the stop خُسْرْ, raa is sakin after sakin sin; the vowel before them is damma on kha, so heavy.

teach.heading: Ayah 3 rules
bullets: illal-ladhina: lam merges, shaddah on laam
teach.note: Be precise: آمَنُوا has hamzah then madd letter in the same word: this is madd badal, normally read at 2 counts. Do not call it muttasil. Ask pupils what the difference is: in muttasil the hamzah comes after the madd letter.

teach.heading: Ayah 3, second half
teach.note: Point out the final alif after waw in تَوَاصَوْا is not pronounced. The waw is sakin after fatha. Stop on الصَّبْر: raa sakin, ba sakin before it, sad has fatha so tafkhim. Ask pupils to say it with a full mouth.

teach.heading: Stopping points
bullets: Start again at the next ayah
Do not stop in the middle of a phrase
teach.note: Remind pupils that stopping at ayah ends is the best practice. Starting mid-ayah is allowed if breath runs out, but go back to a sensible word. Practise one stop in the middle of ayah 3 after وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ and restart.

practice: Which type of lam is in الْعَصْرِ?
Why is the raa heavy when you stop on خُسْرٍ?
Is آمَنُوا madd muttasil or badal? Explain.
independent: Recite Al-'Asr three times, marking each rule
Record yourself and listen back
Peer assess using the checklist
exit: How do you stop on الصَّبْر?
lessons.homework: Memorise Surat Al-'Asr securely and recite it to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: audio support, chunked lines. Stretch: add explanations of each rule in writing.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surat Al-'Asr
lessons.title: Surat Al-'Asr: meaning and reflection
objectives: Explain the oath and the four conditions
Link the surah to daily life
Reflect on how we use our time

keywords.def: a solemn statement swearing by something

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-'Asr.
What does khusr mean?

teach.heading: The oath by time
bullets: 'Asr means time, or the late afternoon
teach.note: Explain that Allah swears by what He wills, and that scholars mention both time and the late afternoon as meanings. Do not claim one only. Ask: what does swearing by time tell us about its value?

teach.heading: Humanity in loss
teach.note: Stress the 'unless'. The exception that follows shows that loss is not the final answer. Ask: where do we see loss in life? Wasted time, wasted talent, wasted chance. Keep this simple and uplifting.

teach.heading: The four conditions
teach.note: Write the four in order on the board and tie each to the Arabic: آمَنُوا، عَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ، تَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ، تَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ. Note that the last two are community actions: we do not rescue ourselves alone.

teach.heading: Living the surah
teach.note: Ask pupils to give one example of 'tawasaw bil-haqq' (a friend reminding you to pray) and 'tawasaw bis-sabr' (encouraging a friend to continue revising). Discuss how to give advice gently. Link to the idea that Muslims support one another.

teach.heading: Tadabbur steps
bullets: Ask: what does it ask of me?
teach.note: Teach a three-step tadabbur routine: say it, understand it, apply it. Note that this is a reflection method, not a replacement for a scholar's tafsir. Pupils write one personal action.

practice: What does Allah swear by in the first ayah?
List the four conditions that save from loss.
Why is advising one another so important?
independent: Draw a four-part diagram of the four conditions with an example for each
Write a short paragraph: how I will use my time better
Discuss in pairs: how to give advice with kindness
exit: Give one action you will take from this surah.
lessons.homework: Write a 100-word reflection on Surat Al-'Asr and one practical goal.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: word bank for the four conditions. Stretch: compare the surah with 49:11 on respect between believers.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surat Al-Humazah
lessons.title: Surat Al-Humazah: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Surat Al-Humazah (104)
Identify noon, tanween and meem rules
Stop and restart sensibly

keywords.def: changing noon sakinah to a meem when ba follows

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-'Asr.
Name the iqlab letter.

teach.heading: Listen and recite
bullets: Pupils echo, then recite in pairs
teach.note: Recite: وَيْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ، الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ، يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ، كَلَّا لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ... Keep a measured pace; this is a heavy surah to hear. Maintain a calm tone.

teach.heading: Noon and tanween
teach.note: Show examples: وَيْلٌ لِّكُلِّ (tanween before lam: idghaam bila ghunnah), مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ (tanween before waw: idghaam bi-ghunnah), لَيُنبَذَنَّ (noon before ba: iqlab). Ask pupils to say why. Misconception: using ghunnah on lam.

teach.heading: Meem and silah
teach.note: عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ: meem sakin followed by meem with shaddah, merge with ghunnah. عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍ: tanween then meem. مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ: silah kubra, 4-5 counts. Revise these from Lesson 3.

teach.heading: Hard words
teach.note: Practise الْحُطَمَةِ, تَطَّلِعُ, الْأَفْئِدَةِ slowly. In تَطَّلِعُ the taa is doubled with the taa that follows (tatta-li'u). Pupils pronounce the doubled sound firmly. Check each shaddah is held clearly.

teach.heading: Stops
bullets: On mumaddadah: stop with a sakin haa
teach.note: The last ayah ends in a taa marbutah with tanween kasra, so we stop on a sakin haa: mumaddadah. The same for al-hutamah in ayah 4. Remind pupils of the difference from tanween 'iwad. Practise restarting at ayah 4.

practice: Which rule is in لَيُنبَذَنَّ?
Which rule joins عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ?
How do you stop on مُّمَدَّدَةٍ?
independent: Recite ayat 1-5 and mark every noon and meem rule
Recite ayat 6-9 with a partner
Self-assess with the checklist
exit: Name one iqlab word in the surah.
Why is there silah kubra in مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ?
lessons.homework: Learn ayat 1-5 of Al-Humazah and recite them tomorrow.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and colour key. Stretch: teach the rules to a partner.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surat Al-Humazah
lessons.title: Surat Al-Humazah: meaning and adab with speech
objectives: Explain the meaning of each ayah
Connect the surah with respectful speech
Reflect on attachment to wealth

keywords.def: speaking about someone in a way they would dislike
the Crusher, a name for a place in the Fire

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite ayat 1-5.
What is idghaam mithlayn?

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3: the warning
bullets: Humazah and lumazah: those who slander and mock
He gathers wealth and counts it again and again
teach.note: Explain that humazah and lumazah both refer to harming people with words, and that scholars give slightly different distinctions; keep it simple. The surah goes on to wealth: counting and hoarding. The next ayah: he thinks his wealth will make him last forever.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-9: the consequence
bullets: He will be thrown into al-Hutamah
It will be closed over them in extended columns
teach.note: Read the translation slowly. Emphasise that these are strong words which should make us reflect, not frighten us for no reason. Ask: what is the link between the first three ayat and these ones?

teach.heading: The tongue
teach.note: Read the meaning of 49:11: let not a people mock another people. And 49:12: do not spy on one another or backbite. A hadith in Sahih Muslim defines ghibah as mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes. Discuss: why is it hard to avoid backbiting?

teach.heading: Wealth and the heart
bullets: Wealth is a test, not a goal
Gratitude and generosity are the cure
teach.note: Avoid saying wealth is bad. The surah criticises hoarding and false security. Ask pupils how generosity might be the opposite. Link to Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur from Year 8.

teach.heading: My personal action
bullets: One word I will stop using
One kind word I will say daily
A dua for a clean tongue
teach.note: Pupils write their action privately. No sharing is required. Close with a dua for protecting our tongues and our hearts from harm.

practice: What does humazah mean?
What false belief does the person have in ayah 3?
Which ayah of Surat Al-Hujurat forbids backbiting?
independent: Write a one-paragraph tafsir summary of ayat 1-4
Create a 'Think before you speak' checklist
Discuss in pairs: when is it okay to mention someone's fault? (advice, not gossip)
exit: Give two meanings of the surah in your own words.
State one action to protect your tongue.
lessons.homework: Write about one situation where you can practise kind speech this week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: simple translation chart with key words. Stretch: compare with Surat Al-Ma'un in 150 words.

lessons.unit: Unit 5: Surat Al-Fil
lessons.title: Surat Al-Fil: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Surat Al-Fil (105)
Identify rules in each ayah
Practise stops and hamzah
starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Humazah.
What is iqlab?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
teach.note: Recite: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ، أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ، وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ، تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ مِّن سِجِّيلٍ، فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولٍ. Model slowly.

teach.heading: Noon and tanween rules
teach.note: طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ: tanween then hamzah, so clear. حِجَارَةٍ مِّن: tanween then meem, idghaam bi-ghunnah. مِن سِجِّيلٍ: noon sakin before sin, ikhfa. Ask why. كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولٍ: tanween then meem, idghaam bi-ghunnah.

teach.heading: Soft yaa in kayfa and kaydahum
bullets: Yaa sakinah after fatha is a leen letter
teach.note: كَيْفَ and كَيْدَهُمْ have yaa sakinah after fatha. Madd leen only appears when the next letter is sakin because we stop. Here the next letter has its own vowel, so no lengthening. Ask: how is this different from stopping on قُرَيْشٍ?

teach.heading: Madd and the end
teach.note: Stopping on تَضْلِيلٍ: madd 'arid. Stopping on مَأْكُولٍ: waw madd followed by lam sakin by stop, so 2, 4 or 6. Recall consistency. Mention the hamzah in مَأْكُولٍ is a hamzah sakinah after meem fatha.

teach.heading: Self-check
teach.note: Pupils read, partner marks. Teacher circulates. Listen for the doubled jeem in سِجِّيلٍ, the clear kaf in كَيْفَ and the heavy letters in طَيْرًا and تَضْلِيلٍ.

practice: Which rule applies to طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ?
Which rule applies to مِن سِجِّيلٍ?
Stop on مَأْكُولٍ. Which madd, how many counts?
independent: Recite Al-Fil three times, marking each rule
Record a recitation and compare with a model
Peer assess with the checklist
exit: Name two noon/tanween rules in Al-Fil.
lessons.homework: Learn all of Surat Al-Fil securely.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: audio chunks and rule key. Stretch: explain every rule aloud for ayah 4.

lessons.unit: Unit 5: Surat Al-Fil
lessons.title: Surat Al-Fil: meaning and lessons
objectives: Explain the meaning of each ayah
Describe the historical setting without adding detail the Qur'an does not give
Draw out lessons about trust in Allah

keywords.def: relying on Allah while taking the means

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Fil.
What is idghaam bi-ghunnah?

teach.heading: Ayat 1-2: Do you not see?
bullets: Alam tara: have you not seen?
Allah dealt with the people of the elephant
Their plan was brought to nothing
teach.note: Explain that the question is for the Prophet ﷺ and for us to reflect on. The Qur'an says Allah made their plan go astray (fi tadlil). Ask: what is a scheme? What does it mean for it to fail completely?

teach.heading: Ayat 3-5: What happened
bullets: They struck with stones of baked clay
He made them like eaten-up chaff
teach.note: Stay with the Qur'an's wording: tayran ababil, hijaratin min sijjil, ka'asfin ma'kul. Do not add details such as the shape or size of the birds, since the surah does not give them. Ask: what image does 'chaff' create?

teach.heading: Historical setting
bullets: Seerah sources name Abrahah and his army
They marched against the Ka'bah in Makkah
This became known as the Year of the Elephant
teach.note: Say clearly that Abrahah's name comes from historical (seerah) sources, not from the Qur'an text. Well-known tradition says the Prophet ﷺ was born in that year. Separate what the Qur'an says from what reports add. Ask: why does this distinction matter?

teach.heading: Lessons
bullets: Allah protects His House and His religion
Power and numbers are not everything
Trust Allah and do what is right
teach.note: Discuss tawakkul: relying on Allah while taking the means. Ask pupils for an example from daily life (revising and making dua). Link to Surat Quraysh which follows Al-Fil in the mushaf, which reminds Quraysh to worship the Lord of this House.

teach.heading: Reflect
bullets: Where do we meet arrogance today?
How should we respond with humility?
A dua for protection and humility
teach.note: Pupils write one sentence on pride versus humility. Keep discussion general, not political. Close with a dua asking Allah to protect us and keep our hearts humble.

practice: What does 'fi tadlil' mean?
Name two details the Qur'an gives about the birds' attack.
Does the Qur'an name the leader of the army? Explain.
independent: Write a summary of each ayah in your own words
Draw a storyboard of ayat 3-5
Write a short paragraph on tawakkul
exit: What is one lesson from Al-Fil?
What is the difference between what the Qur'an says and what history adds?
lessons.homework: Write a 100-word reflection linking Al-Fil and Quraysh.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture-supported translation. Stretch: compare Al-Fil with another surah on divine protection.

lessons.unit: Unit 6: Recital and reflection
lessons.title: Recital assessment and reflection
objectives: Recite one chosen surah from the half term with accuracy
Self-assess and peer-assess against the rubric
Set targets for Year 10

keywords.def: a set of criteria for judging quality

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Recite Al-Fatihah.
Which surah will you recite today and why?

teach.heading: Prepare
bullets: Check noon, meem and madd rules
Take a calm breath and begin
teach.note: Give pupils five minutes to prepare quietly. Remind them of adab: calm, clean place, a dua. Reduce nerves with encouragement and remind them of the hadith narrated by A'ishah that the one who struggles in recitation has a double reward.

teach.heading: Rubric
teach.note: Share the rubric with levels. Pupils recite individually in breakout rooms or in the main room. Mark with the rubric. Stress that the teacher gives one strength, one target and one action.

teach.heading: Recite and listen
teach.note: In pairs, pupils recite, then listen. Use sentence stems: 'One strength was...', 'One target is...'. Keep the atmosphere supportive.

teach.heading: Revision plan
teach.note: Show a simple revision cycle: new, recent, old. Pupils write a plan for the next two weeks. Link this with Year 8's long-term memorisation work.

teach.heading: Reflect
teach.note: Pupils write a short reflection. Share one thing aloud. Close with a dua for sincerity, steadfastness and love of the Qur'an.

practice: Which rule is most secure for you?
Which rule needs more work?
independent: Recite your chosen surah for assessment
Complete peer feedback with the rubric
Write a reflection and three targets
lessons.homework: Practise your targets daily and record a new recitation next week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: simplified rubric with sentence stems. Stretch: coach another pupil on one rule.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Muddaththir and madd in recitation
lessons.title: Surat Al-Muddaththir 74:1-10: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: 'O you who covers himself, arise and warn!' These words came early in the Prophet's ﷺ mission. What do they ask of him, and of us?
objectives: To memorise Al-Muddaththir 74:1-10 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 74:1-10 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 74:1-10 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 74:1-10 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: standing up for the truth with patience and purity

keywords.def: the one wrapped in a cloak

hook.text: 'O you who covers himself, arise and warn!' These words came early in the Prophet's ﷺ mission. What do they ask of him, and of us?
hook.a: To stand up for the message: magnify Allah, purify oneself, avoid wrong, be patient for Allah (74:1 to 7).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O you who covers himself, arise and warn, and your Lord glorify, and your clothing purify, and uncleanliness avoid' (Al-Muddaththir 74:1 to 5). These are among the earliest ayat revealed after the first revelation (Bukhari).

starter.q: How many ayat are in Surat Al-Muddaththir (سورة المدثر)?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Muddaththir 74:1-10
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 74:1-10 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُدَّثِّرُ (١) قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ (٢) وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ (٣) وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ (٤) وَٱلرُّجْزَ فَٱهْجُرْ (٥) وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ (٦) وَلِرَبِّكَ فَٱصْبِرْ (٧) فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِى ٱلنَّاقُورِ (٨) فَذَٰلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ (٩) عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍۢ (١٠)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: O you who covers himself [with a garment], Arise and warn
And your Lord glorify And your clothing purify
And uncleanliness avoid And do not confer favor to acquire more
But for your Lord be patient. And when the trumpet is blown,
That Day will be a difficult day For the disbelievers - not easy.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 74:1-10 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Which command is NOT in 74:2 to 7?
check.why: 74:2 to 7: arise and warn, glorify your Lord, purify your clothing, avoid uncleanliness, do not give to gain more, be patient for your Lord.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Muddaththir 74:1-10 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 74:1-10 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 74:1-10. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

practice.a: ikhfa

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 74:1-10 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: In the portal box, list the six commands in 74:2 to 7 and one modern way to live each.
independent.a: Arise and warn; glorify Allah; purify clothing; avoid uncleanliness; give without seeking more; be patient: each with a sensible example.

independent.q: Explain how 74:6 'do not confer favour to acquire more' links to sincerity.
independent.a: Give for Allah, not to get more back; that is ikhlas.

exit.q: Al-Muddaththir 74:3: «وَرَبَّكَ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: فَكَبِّرْ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: 'O you who covers himself, arise and warn!' These words came early in the Prophet's ﷺ mission. What do they ask of him, and of us?
exit.a: To stand up for the message: magnify Allah, purify oneself, avoid wrong, be patient for Allah (74:1 to 7).

lessons.homework: Recite Al-Muddaththir 74:1-10 to a parent three times a day and revise Al-Mulk to Nuh (67 to 71) on the rota; tick the portal revision log each day.
lessons.send: SEND: shorter chunks (one ayah), the pupil PDF with each word spaced, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: link to the next ayat and explain one rule to the class.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Muddaththir and madd in recitation
lessons.title: Madd tabi'i and madd muttasil
lessons.bigQuestion: If a reciter stretched the same madd 2 counts in one ayah and 6 in the next, what would you notice?
objectives: To understand how the natural madd (2 counts) and the joined madd (4 or 5 counts) work and keep their lengths consistent
successCriteria: All: identify madd letters and stretch them 2 counts
Most: recognise madd muttasil and stretch 4 or 5
Some: explain why one length must be kept throughout a recitation
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the measured, even recitation passed down through teachers

keywords.def: lengthening a vowel sound, counted in beats (harakat)
joined madd: hamza in the same word, 4 or 5

hook.text: If a reciter stretched the same madd 2 counts in one ayah and 6 in the next, what would you notice?
hook.a: It would sound uneven; lengths must be consistent, as reciters were taught.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). Even lengths are part of tartil.

starter.q: Recite Al-Muddaththir 74:4 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

starter.a: the time to fold one finger
options: the time to fold one finger

teach.heading: The family of madd
teach.note: Bismillah. Today: the first two rows; the rest come over the half term.

head: Madd
When
Counts (Hafs)
Example
rows: Madd letter, nothing after it causes more
Hamza after the madd letter, same word
Stopping on the letter after a madd letter

teach.heading: Madd tabi'i: the natural madd
bullets: ا after fathah, و after dammah, ي after kasrah
No hamza or sukoon after it
teach.note: Model ثِيَابَكَ (74:4), ٱلنَّاقُورِ (74:8): exactly 2 counts.

teach.heading: Madd muttasil: joined
bullets: Madd letter then hamza in the same word
Choose one length and keep it
teach.note: Examples in Al-Muddaththir: يَشَآءُ (74:31), شَآءَ (74:37), يَتَسَآءَلُونَ (74:40), ٱلْخَآئِضِينَ (74:45). The sign ٓ over the madd letter shows it is longer than natural.

misconception.wrong: shaa'a with 2 counts, like a natural madd
misconception.right: shaaaa'a: 4 or 5 counts, because hamza follows in the same word

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Alif then hamza in the same word: madd muttasil.

practice.q: Mark and count every madd in 74:37 «لِمَن شَآءَ مِنكُمْ أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ».
practice.a: شَآءَ muttasil 4 or 5; no other madd letters stretched (أَوْ is leen only at a stop).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Leave Me with the one I created alone And to whom I granted extensive wealth And children present [with him]
And spread [everything] before him, easing [his life]. Then he desires that I should add more. No! Indeed, he has been toward Our verses obstinate.
I will cover him with arduous torment. Indeed, he thought and deliberated. So may he be destroyed [for] how he deliberated.
Then may he be destroyed [for] how he deliberated. Then he considered [again]; Then he frowned and scowled;
Then he turned back and was arrogant And said, "This is not but magic imitated [from others]. This is not but the word of a human being."
I will drive him into Saqar. And what can make you know what is Saqar? It lets nothing remain and leaves nothing [unburned],
Blackening the skins. Over it are nineteen [angels].

hook.text: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ not to rush his tongue when receiving the Qur'an: 'upon Us is its collection' (75:16 to 17). What does this teach us about how to memorise?
hook.a: Listen first, then follow (75:18); trust Allah, be calm, do not rush.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Move not your tongue with it, [O Muhammad], to hasten with recitation of the Qur'an.' This is the root of talaqqi: listen, then follow.
